sentences.text:
Order 
The appellant/insurance company has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 30.08.2014 passed in claim case No.515/2013 whereby challenging its liability to pay compensation.
2. The short facts of the case are that on 22.09.2009 at around 04 O'clock in the evening the respondent was going as a pillion rider by sitting on the motorcycle of his relative to Ujjain.
The respondent No.2 was driving Tempo registration number MP13-T-1009 of his ownership.
When the respondent No.1 reached near Raaghau Piplyaa Fanta near Devdharm Temple, Ujjain the said Tempo dashed into the motorcycle of respondent No.1 because of which she sustained grievous injuries.
3. The claim petition was filed by her under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the claims tribunal.

The claims tribunal after considering the evidence available on record concluded that the accident was a result of rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle, thus, a total compensation of Rs.1,74,713/- was awarded to the respondent No.1 and the appellant / insurance company was held NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28788 2 MA-2117-2014 responsible for payment of compensation.

The singular ground which has been taken by the appellant/insurance company in the present appeal is that the driver of the insured vehicle at the time of accident was not having licence for driving the transport vehicle, thus, he was not eligible to drive the insured vehicle, which is a Tempo.
He thus prays for exoneration of the insurance company from liability of payment of compensation.

sentences.text: The submission of the learned counsel for the appellant has now been already discarded by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a recent judgment delivered on 06.11.2024 in the case Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Rambha Devi and others (Civil Appeal No.841/2018).

entities.text: Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Rambha Devi and others (Civil Appeal No.841/2018)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that a person who is holding LMV licence can also drive transport vehicle under 7500 kgs.
It is not the case of the appellant/insurance company that the vehicle in question was being more than 7500 kgs.

It is also not under dispute that the driver of the insured vehicle at the relevant time was having LMV licence,
5.
Considering the same, this contention holds no water, consequently, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
